data.note:
Specimen s_93883f5fd7 = colchicine confirmed: PubChem CID 6167, C22H25NO6, ChEMBL107 Tubulin inhibitor, BBBC021 annotation Microtubule destabilizers - agreement verified (e17).

My blinded call Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.72) scored correct by code. Reflection:

Evidence converged at high dose: w_6786be54b3 3µM showed severe nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity z -36.0, nuc_form_factor -13.2), act_tub_ratio 8.52, act_mean 6.38 with dim green tubulin, cell loss (cell_count z -3.79) and multinucleation proxy 3.68 (e4,e13). Dose-responses were decisive: tub_mean Spearman -1.0 p=0.0 (1.26 at 0.1µM to -5.11 at 3µM, e10), cell_count -1.0 p=0.0 (e11), frac_multinucleate_proxy +1.0 p=0.0 (e12). Intermediate doses showed mitotic-like increase (e3,e5,e9) consistent with spindle poison arrest, later lost to cytotoxicity at 3µM.

Atlas: NSC vote Microtubule destabilizers 1/4 but that vote had highest similarity 0.77 at 3µM; k-neighbours 5/10 destabilizers (nocodazole, vincristine, demecolcine), 4/10 stabilizers (epothilone B, docetaxel), mean similarities 0.325 vs 0.378 (e6). The monotonic tubulin loss and multinucleation pattern resolved the split toward destabilizers over stabilizers, Actin disruptors, Aurora/Eg5, Kinase inhibitors.

Literature: colchicine-site binders are canonical microtubule-destabilizing agents distinct from stabilizers (e.g. PMID 24530796 BAL27862 binds colchicine site with distinct effects on microtubule organization; PMID 35939994 novel fragment-derived colchicine-site binders as microtubule-destabilizing agents; PMID 28640209 quinolin-6-yloxyacetamides are microtubule destabilizing agents that bind to the colchicine site). ChEMBL mechanism Tubulin inhibitor matches.

Budget 4/4 used strategically; no further wells needed, though low-dose replicates would have strengthened NSC margin.

Dossier complete.

reflection.text:
This was a correct call - colchicine unblinded as Tubulin inhibitor via ChEMBL CHEMBL2095182 with name and BBBC021 structure agreeing (e16, e17), consistent with colchicine-site binders being classified as microtubule-destabilizing agents PMID 35939994, PMID 24530796, PMID 28640209 - but the evidence was graded, not clean majority, and required weighting dose-order over vote count.

What got right:

1. Acquisition strategy spanning threshold: listing showed 8 doses (0.001-3 uM) with 4 wells left (e1). We sampled 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 uM (e2-e5) which formed a coherent onset-to-maximum series per the review. That allowed monotonic trends to emerge despite single-well-per-dose sampling.

2. Tubulin intensity directionality was decisive. e2 at 1 uM already showed tub_mean z=-2.7 and tub_glcm_contrast z=-2.5 with nuc_area z=+3.0. e4 at 3 uM showed tubulin strongly down in context of nuc_solidity z=-36.0, nuc_form_factor z=-13.2, nuc_area z=-9.2. Dose_response e10 quantified this as Spearman rho=-1.00 (p=0) for tub_mean, falling from +1.26 to -5.11 as noted in the critique. A microtubule stabilizer should preserve or raise and bundle tubulin signal; the monotonic loss directly favored destabilizer and was listed as contradicting stabilizer in the hypothesis update (e14, e6 contradicting e10/e4). e11 cell_count rho=-1.00 and e12 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+1.00 and e13 lower density vs DMSO provided consistent cytotoxic / aberrant mitosis context.

3. Comparison to reference atlas was interpreted correctly by similarity, not just vote count. e6 NSC vote was 1/4 Microtubule destabilizers with k-neighbours 5/10 destabilizers, 4/10 stabilizers, 1/10 Actin disruptors. The per-well truth tallies show why the 1/4 is misleading: w_9162c8299a 0.1 uM nearest Microtubule stabilizers similarity 0.267, w_000d834b64 0.3 uM Actin disruptors 0.194, w_4bd26081f9 1 uM Kinase inhibitors 0.20, but w_6786be54b3 3 uM Microtubule destabilizers similarity 0.77. We based the submission on the high-dose/high-similarity well plus internal trends outweighing mixed low-dose low-similarity votes, which the unblinding confirms (protocol votes 1 each, summed similarity 0.77 for destabilizers).

What misled or was weak and why:

1. Low-dose morphology mimics other classes. e3 at 0.1 uM: nuc_area z=+4.3, nuc_dna_mean z=+3.1, act_mean z=+2.5. Enlarged nuclei with increased DNA texture and apparent actin increase can resemble stabilizer or actin phenotypes at threshold, which is exactly what the atlas returned at 0.1-0.3 uM. e5 at 0.3 uM: frac_mitotic_like z=+2.2 but tub_glcm_contrast z=+1.7 and nuc_major_axis z=-1.5 was near-baseline, weakening any single-well call. e7 nuc_area rho=-0.80 (p=0.2) captures the biphasic pattern: enlarged at low dose, collapsed at high dose (-9.2). Without dose ordering this looks incoherent.

2. Isolated actin signal. e3 act_mean z=+2.5 raised Actin disruptor hypothesis (e6 1/10, e14 p=0.06). e8 dose_response act_mean rho=+0.20 (p=0.8) contradicted a true actin mechanism and was used to downweight it, but single-well actin fluorescence is noisy and texture dependent.

3. Mitotic fraction non-monotonicity. e9 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.20 (p=0.8) despite e5 z=+2.2. At 3 uM with fragmented/micronucleus-like nuclei and low solidity, mitotic classification breaks down, so a flat rho is expected rather than evidence against destabilizers. Eg5/Aurora alternatives were kept in hypothesis board at p=0.04/0.03 precisely because e12 multinucleation alone does not distinguish them, only e10 tubulin loss does.

4. Measurement and acquisition limitations. All dose_responses are n=4 wells, so Spearman p-values are underpowered (e7 p=0.2, e8 p=0.8, e9 p=0.8) except the perfect monotonic tub_mean/cell_count/multinucleate signals. describe_phenotype e13 returned only "density lower vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: unknown" - non-specific and not independently diagnostic. Sampling only one replicate per dose means we cannot assess well-to-well variability, as the review flagged in approving despite insufficient replication.

Why the conclusion was still warranted: The direction of three independent monotonic readouts (tubulin loss, cell count loss, multinucleate rise) plus the extreme nuclear solidity collapse at maximal dose aligns with destabilizer-induced depolymerization, G2/M failure and micronucleation/fragmentation, while stabilizer, actin disruptor and kinase-inhibitor alternatives predict opposite or flat tubulin trends. Literature search for colchicine tubulin mechanism returned 5/47 hits (e18) and for phenotype linkage returned 0 hits (e19), so the call rested on imaging dose-response and atlas similarity, later verified by compound lookup.

Calibration lesson: p=0.72 in e14/e15 was overconfident for a 1/4 majority with single-well sampling. The review estimate of 0.50-0.65 for the top class specifically is more appropriate; we should have explicitly cited the split vote and replicate limitation as uncertainty. Next experiment as proposed - EB3-GFP repolymerization washout with phospho-H3 and spindle multipolarity vs reference destabilizer/stabilizer controls at 0.1,1,3 uM - would test depolymerization kinetics directly rather than relying on fixed-cell tubulin mean.

No clinical implications are discussed - this is retrospective cell-imaging assay validation only.

Eg5/Aurora alternatives were kept in hypothesis board at p=0.04/0.03 precisely because e12 multinucleation alone does not distinguish them, only e10 tubulin loss does.

4. Measurement and acquisition limitations. All dose_responses are n=4 wells, so Spearman p-values are underpowered (e7 p=0.2, e8 p=0.8, e9 p=0.8) except the perfect monotonic tub_mean/cell_count/multinucleate signals. describe_phenotype e13 returned only "density lower vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: unknown" - non-specific and not independently diagnostic. Sampling only one replicate per dose means we cannot assess well-to-well variability, as the review flagged in approving despite insufficient replication.

Why the conclusion was still warranted: The direction of three independent monotonic readouts (tubulin loss, cell count loss, multinucleate rise) plus the extreme nuclear solidity collapse at maximal dose aligns with destabilizer-induced depolymerization, G2/M failure and micronucleation/fragmentation, while stabilizer, actin disruptor and kinase-inhibitor alternatives predict opposite or flat tubulin trends. Literature search for colchicine tubulin mechanism returned 5/47 hits (e18) and for phenotype linkage returned 0 hits (e19), so the call rested on imaging dose-response and atlas similarity, later verified by compound lookup.

Calibration lesson: p=0.72 in e14/e15 was overconfident for a 1/4 majority with single-well sampling. The review estimate of 0.50-0.65 for the top class specifically is more appropriate; we should have explicitly cited the split vote and replicate limitation as uncertainty. Next experiment as proposed - EB3-GFP repolymerization washout with phospho-H3 and spindle multipolarity vs reference destabilizer/stabilizer controls at 0.1,1,3 uM - would test depolymerization kinetics directly rather than relying on fixed-cell tubulin mean.

No clinical implications are discussed - this is retrospective cell-imaging assay validation only.

- e10 rho=-1.00 tubulin loss monotonic from +1.26 to -5.11 contradicted stabilizer hypothesis
